node.title: Re: Preserving newlines with Web::Scraper
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
It seems that [mod://Web::Scraper] uses [mod://HTML::TreeBuilder::XPath], and [mod://HTML::TreeBuilder] has an no_space_compacting option that is disabled by default, causing that module to [https://metacpan.org/source/KENTNL/HTML-Tree-5.07/lib/HTML/TreeBuilder.pm#L1304|do] s/[\n\r\f\t ]+/ /g by default. At the moment I don't see a way to set arbitrary options on the parser via [mod://Web::Scraper], this is probably worth opening an [https://github.com/miyagawa/web-scraper/issues|issue] for.

Two workarounds I see at the moment: replacing [mod://Web::Scraper] with [mod://Web::Scraper::LibXML] works for me:

use warnings; use strict; use Data::Dump; use Web::Scraper::LibXML; my $scraper = scraper { process '//p[contains(@class, "myClass")]', 'paragraph' => 'TEXT'; }; dd $scraper->scrape(\<<'END_HTML');

Blah Blah Blah

END_HTML __END__ { paragraph => "Blah\n\nBlah\n\nBlah\n" }

Or, monkey-patching [https://metacpan.org/source/MIYAGAWA/Web-Scraper-0.38/lib/Web/Scraper.pm#L112|Web::Scraper::build_tree]:

*Web::Scraper::build_tree = sub { my($self, $html) = @_; my $t = HTML::TreeBuilder::XPath->new; $t->store_comments(1) if ($t->can('store_comments')); $t->no_space_compacting(1); $t->ignore_unknown(0); $t->parse($html); $t->eof; $t; };
